## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cara Sutta* ("Walking", Iti 110; It 4.11, PTS It 115) is a discourse located in the fourth division (*Catukkanipāta*) of the *Itivuttaka* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The discourse addresses what it means for a monastic to practice with ardency and compunction while walking and across bodily postures [SuttaCentral]. On SuttaCentral, sixteen translations across fourteen languages are recorded, including an English rendering by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies an exact full parallel in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, namely AN 4.11 (likewise named *Carasutta*) [SuttaCentral]. Computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus strongly confirms this parallel, finding 132 matches totaling 33,883 shared characters between the two texts, including a primary alignment covering Iti 110 §2.1–12.6 and AN 4.11 §11.0.3–11.11.6 at 0.93 similarity [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects substantial internal Pali reuse with the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), the immediately following *Sampannasīla Sutta* (Iti 111), the *Ekādasakanipāta* (AN 11), the *Mahāgopālaka Sutta* (MN 33), and the commentary *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Automated cross-language alignments include matches in the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) as well as the Tibetan *Saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna* (D0287) and *Aṣṭasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā* (D0012) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
